q: Our buyer says our carbon figure is higher than the database value. What do we say?
title: Our figure vs the database: explaining it
short: Database values are averages for a region or technology, often older and with a different boundary. Your figure comes from your own bills. Show the boundary, factors and period behind yours, and point out which differences are real: fuel type, grid share, yield. A measured figure usually beats an average.
audience: Suppliers whose measured figures differ from buyer databases

ul: Materials included in one but not the other?

p: If yours is higher for a real reason, such as diesel generator use, say what you plan to do about it. If it is a boundary mismatch, line them up.

senseible: Senseible reads bills, fuel invoices and production records into dated, fingerprinted records, so the figure you send a buyer can be traced to its documents.

sources.label: GHG Protocol Corporate Value Chain (Scope 3) Standard
